app.tagline: Reads your computer, explains what it finds, changes nothing without asking.

agent.platform.unsupported: The SupportOne agent runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. This computer is not one of them.

check.unknown.needs_admin: This check needs administrator rights to read what it reads.
check.os.info.ok: Running %s %s. It has been on for %s.
check.hardware.inventory.unreported: This computer does not report its make and model. It has a %s (%d cores).
check.hardware.ram.low: Only %s of memory. A current operating system and a few browser tabs will feel slow on this; more memory is the single biggest improvement you could make.
check.battery.health.absent: No battery — this is a desktop computer.
check.battery.health.ok: The battery is in good shape: it still holds %d%% of the charge it held when new.
check.battery.health.worn: The battery holds %d%% of the charge it held when new. It will not last as long away from a charger; plan to replace it.
check.battery.health.failing: The battery holds only %d%% of the charge it held when new and should be replaced.
check.battery.health.unreadable: There is a battery, but this computer does not report enough about it to judge its health.
check.disk.volumes.ok: %d drives checked. The one with the least room, %s, still has %s free.
check.disk.volumes.low: %s is running low on room: %s free (%s%%). Clearing space now avoids trouble later.
check.disk.volumes.critical: %s is nearly full: %s free (%s%%). At this level programs start failing to save files.
check.disk.volumes.none: No drives could be read on this computer.
check.disk.smart.ok.one: %d drive checked, and it reports itself healthy.
check.disk.smart.failing: The drive %s reports that it is failing. Back up your files now and plan to replace it.
check.disk.smart.bad_spots: The drive %s has %d bad spots it has had to stop using. It still works, but this is how a disk begins to fail: back up your files and keep an eye on it.
check.disk.smart.unknown: No drive would report its health. That is normal for USB drives and some laptops, and is not a sign of a problem.
check.disk.smart.no_disks: No drives were found to check.

check.network.config.no_address: This computer has no network address, so it is not connected to any network.
check.network.config.no_gateway: Connected on %s, but there is no route out to the internet. Other devices in the building may work; websites will not.
check.network.config.no_dns: Connected on %s, but no DNS server is set, so website names cannot be looked up.
check.network.config.interfaces_unreadab: The network connections could not be read.
check.drivers.problem.ok: Every device reports that it is working.
check.drivers.problem.not_applicable: This check only applies to Windows, which is where devices report an error state.

wizard.outcome.fixed: Something was wrong, it was repaired, and checking again confirmed it.
wizard.outcome.unresolved: Something is still wrong. What was found, and what was tried, is listed below for whoever helps you next.
wizard.outcome.unverified: A change was made that this tool cannot check the effect of. Try the thing that was not working and see.
wizard.outcome.no_fault: Every question SupportOne knows how to ask came back clean. The problem is real; this tool cannot see the cause of it.
wizard.outcome.stopped: You ended this before it finished. Nothing further was changed.
wizard.step.applied: The change was made. Whether it helped is something only trying again can tell.
wizard.step.no_help: The repair was applied and the same problem is still here.
wizard.step.declined: You chose not to change this.
wizard.step.blocked: This could not be repaired from here.

wizard.connection.link.advice: Check that Wi-Fi is switched on and joined to a network, or that the network cable is plugged in at both ends. If it is, restart the router and try again.

check.performance.load.ok: %s of %s memory free, and nothing is queueing for the processor.
check.performance.load.busy: The processor has been busy: %.2f jobs waiting across %d cores over the last minute.
check.performance.load.busy_now: The processor was %d%% busy at the moment this was read. That is one reading, not a pattern — it may just have been doing something.
check.performance.load.memory_low: Only %s of %s memory is free. There is little headroom for anything else you open.
check.performance.load.memory_critical: Almost no memory is free: %s of %s. The computer is working around this constantly, which is what makes it feel slow.
check.performance.load.swapping: The computer has moved %s out of memory onto the disk to keep going. That is much slower than memory.
check.performance.load.unreadable: SupportOne could not read how busy this computer is.
check.backup.status.stale: %s last backed up %s ago. Anything changed since then is not in a backup.
check.backup.status.very_stale: %s last backed up %s ago. More than a month of work is not backed up anywhere SupportOne can see.
check.backup.status.never_run: %s is set up but SupportOne cannot find a completed backup from it.
check.backup.status.none: SupportOne found no %s backup on this computer. It does not see other backup tools, so this does not prove there is no backup — but if you are not sure, that is worth checking.
check.backup.status.unreadable: SupportOne read a %s backup date it does not believe, so it will not report one. The computer's clock may be wrong.
check.backup.status.not_applicable: This computer's system has no single backup tool SupportOne knows how to read, so it did not look. That is not a finding about whether you have a backup.
explain.unknown.failed: This check ran into something it could not read, so it has no answer to give. That is not the same as finding nothing wrong.
explain.unknown.needs_admin: This answer is behind administrator rights, which SupportOne does not ask for in order to start.
explain.unknown.tool_missing: The tool that answers this is not installed on this computer.
explain.os.info.ok: This is what the computer is running. It is here so a technician does not have to ask.
explain.hardware.inventory.ok: This is what the computer is. It is here so a technician does not have to ask.
explain.hardware.inventory.unreported: The computer does not report a model name. Virtual machines and many small boards do not, and it means nothing about how well it works.
explain.hardware.ram.ok: There is enough memory installed for ordinary work.
explain.hardware.ram.low: This computer has less memory than a current desktop system comfortably needs. It will feel slow when several things are open at once, and no setting changes that.
explain.battery.health.ok: The battery still holds close to what it was built to hold.
explain.battery.health.absent: No battery is fitted. On a desktop that is normal.
explain.battery.health.worn: Batteries lose capacity with every charge; this one has lost enough to notice. It is wear, not a fault, and the computer is not in danger.
explain.battery.health.failing: The battery holds less than half of what it was built to hold. It may shut the computer down without warning even when it shows charge remaining.
explain.battery.health.unreadable: A battery is fitted but does not report enough to judge its condition.
explain.disk.volumes.ok: There is room to work on every drive.
explain.disk.volumes.none: No drives could be measured, so there is nothing to report about free space.
explain.disk.volumes.low: A drive is filling up. Below roughly a tenth free, the operating system runs out of room to work in and everything slows down.
explain.disk.volumes.critical: A drive is nearly full. At this point the computer cannot reliably save files, install updates, or even shut down cleanly.
explain.disk.smart.ok: The drives report their own condition as healthy.
explain.disk.smart.no_disks: No drive reported its condition. On many machines that means the drive does not expose it, not that anything is wrong.
explain.disk.smart.unknown: The drives' own health data could not be read on this account.
explain.disk.smart.bad_spots: The drive has found areas it can no longer use and has moved the data elsewhere. A few is normal ageing; a growing number is the drive wearing out.
explain.disk.smart.failing: The drive is reporting that it expects to fail. This is the drive's own assessment of itself, and it is the one warning in this report worth acting on today.
explain.network.config.ok: This computer has an address, knows which router to use, and knows where to look up website names.
explain.network.config.no_address: Nothing on this computer has a usable network address, so it cannot reach anything — local or otherwise.
explain.network.config.no_gateway: This computer has an address but no router to send traffic through. Local devices may work; nothing beyond them will.
explain.network.config.no_dns: This computer can reach the network but has nowhere to look up website names. Addresses typed in full may work while names do not.
explain.network.config.interfaces_unread: The list of network connections could not be read.
explain.updates.os.ok: The operating system is up to date as far as its own records show.
explain.updates.os.pending: Updates have been downloaded and are waiting. Most of them only take effect after a restart.
explain.updates.os.stale: It has been a while since this computer applied an update. Security fixes arrive this way.
explain.updates.os.very_stale: This computer has gone a long time without an update. Every fix released since then is missing, including security ones.
explain.updates.os.unknown: The update history could not be read.
explain.startup.items.ok: These programs start themselves when the computer does. Each one adds to how long that takes.
explain.startup.items.none: Nothing beyond the system itself starts automatically.
explain.security.posture.ok: Disk encryption, the firewall and antivirus are all on as far as this account can see.
explain.security.posture.no_encryption: The disk is not encrypted, so anyone who takes the computer can read what is on it by moving the drive to another machine.
explain.security.posture.no_firewall: The firewall is off, so anything on the same network can try to reach this computer directly.
explain.security.posture.no_antivirus: No antivirus is reporting itself as active.
explain.security.posture.several_off: More than one of the basic protections is off. Together they matter more than any one of them does alone.
explain.security.posture.unreadable: Whether these protections are on could not be read from this account. That is not the same as finding them off.
explain.drivers.problem.ok: Windows reports no device in an error state.
explain.drivers.problem.not_applicable: This operating system has no equivalent of a device in an error state, so there was nothing to look at.
explain.drivers.problem.found: Windows has a device it cannot use properly. That is usually a missing or mismatched driver, and the hardware itself is often fine.
explain.eventlog.errors.none: The system log has no errors recorded in the period checked.
explain.eventlog.errors.quiet: A few errors are recorded, which is normal. Every computer logs some.
explain.eventlog.errors.repeated: The same error keeps recurring. A repeating error usually has one cause behind it, and it is worth finding.
explain.eventlog.errors.critical: The log records the computer stopping unexpectedly. That is worth taking seriously even if it has not happened again.
explain.performance.load.ok: The computer is not short of memory and nothing is queueing for the processor.
explain.performance.load.busy: More work is waiting for the processor than it can run at once. If this is a build, an export or a scan, that is the machine doing its job.
explain.performance.load.busy_now: The processor was busy at the moment this was read. One reading cannot tell a problem from ordinary work.
explain.performance.load.memory_low: Memory is nearly used up. The computer will start moving things to the disk to cope, and that is much slower.
explain.performance.load.memory_critical: Memory is effectively gone. This is what makes a computer feel broken when nothing is actually broken.
explain.performance.load.swapping: The computer has run out of memory and is using the disk in its place. Everything is slower while this lasts.
explain.performance.load.unreadable: How busy this computer is could not be read.
explain.backup.status.ok: There is a recent backup from the tool this computer's system ships with.
explain.backup.status.not_applicable: SupportOne knows how to read the backup tool that Windows and macOS ship with, and this system ships none. Whether you have a backup is a question it cannot answer here.
explain.backup.status.none: SupportOne found no backup from the tool this system ships with. It cannot see other backup tools, so this is not proof there is no backup — but if you are unsure, that itself is worth resolving.
explain.backup.status.never_run: A backup is set up but has not completed. That usually means the destination drive has not been connected since it was configured.
explain.backup.status.stale: The backup is out of date. Everything created or changed since it ran exists in one place only.
explain.backup.status.very_stale: The backup is more than a month out of date. If this computer were lost today, a month of work would go with it.
explain.backup.status.unreadable: The recorded backup date is in the future, which cannot be right. Rather than report a date it does not believe, SupportOne reports none.
explain.step.backup_now: Copy anything you would hate to lose to another drive or a cloud folder. Do this before anything else on this list.
explain.step.set_up_backup: Set up a backup that runs on its own. A backup you have to remember to do is one you will forget.
explain.step.check_backup_now: Check whether you already have a backup running that SupportOne cannot see, and if not, arrange one.
explain.step.reconnect_drive: Connect the backup drive, or check the network share is reachable, and let the backup finish.
explain.step.stop_using: Stop using this computer for anything you cannot afford to lose until the drive is replaced.
explain.step.replace_disk: Arrange for the drive to be replaced. A drive reporting this does not recover.
explain.step.watch_disk: Check this again in a week. A count that stays put is ageing; a count that climbs is a drive on its way out.
explain.step.free_space: Free up space until the drive is at least a tenth empty, then check again.
explain.step.empty_bin: Empty the recycle bin or trash. Deleted files sit there taking up room until you do.
explain.step.move_files_off: Move large files you rarely open — videos, photo archives, old projects — to another drive or cloud storage.
explain.step.uninstall_unused: Uninstall programs you no longer use.
explain.step.restart: Restart the computer. Some of this only takes effect after a restart, and a restart clears a great deal on its own.
explain.step.close_programs: Close what you are not using, particularly browser tabs — they are the usual reason memory runs out.
explain.step.reduce_startup: Turn off programs that start with the computer and that you do not need immediately.
explain.step.add_memory: If this keeps happening, more memory is the fix. Nothing in software substitutes for it.
explain.step.check_cable: Check the network cable is in at both ends, or that Wi-Fi is on and joined to a network.
explain.step.restart_router: Restart the router: unplug it, wait ten seconds, plug it back in, and give it two minutes.
explain.step.turn_on_encryption: Turn on disk encryption — BitLocker on Windows, FileVault on macOS. Save the recovery key somewhere that is not this computer.
explain.step.turn_on_firewall: Turn the firewall back on in the system settings.
explain.step.turn_on_antivirus: Turn on the antivirus that came with the system, or check the one you installed is running.
explain.step.replace_battery: Have the battery replaced when it becomes inconvenient. It is a wear item, like tyres.
explain.step.keep_charger: Keep the charger with you until then, and do not rely on the percentage shown.
explain.step.update_drivers: Open Device Manager, find the device marked with a warning, and update its driver.
explain.step.note_when: Note what you were doing when it happened. A pattern is worth more to whoever fixes this than the log entry itself.
explain.step.run_as_admin: Run SupportOne as an administrator and check again. It does not ask for this to start, only for the answers that need it.
explain.step.install_tool: Install the tool named above, then check again.
explain.step.check_again: Check again. If it still cannot answer, the reason above is what to pass on.
explain.step.check_clock: Check the computer's date and time are right.
explain.escalate: This is past what is worth working through alone. Save a report and give it to whoever supports this computer.

explain.updates.installed.recent: This is the list a technician needs to write down what was patched and when. It covers what the record itself covers, and nothing beyond it.
explain.updates.installed.old: Nothing has been applied for a while on this record. Whether that matters depends on what the record covers — it is worth reading alongside the update check above rather than on its own.
explain.updates.installed.none: The machine keeps this record and there is nothing in it. Either updates have genuinely never been applied, or they arrive through a channel this record does not cover.
explain.updates.installed.unreadable: The record either could not be read or carries no dates, so there is no patch history to put in a report.

remote.heading: What a remote-help session lets someone do
remote.can.see_screen: They can see your screen: everything on it, including anything you open by accident.
remote.can.control: They can move your mouse and type on your keyboard as if they were sitting here.
remote.can.read_files: They can open and read any file you can open, including personal ones.
remote.can.act_as_you: Anything they do is done as you: websites you are signed in to are signed in for them too.
remote.cannot.watch: SupportOne cannot watch this session or limit what they do. It only records that you agreed to it and when you said it was over.
remote.end_it: You can end it at any time by closing the remote-help program.
remote.close_anything: Close the remote-help program now if it is still open.
agent.remote.none_known: This build does not know any remote-help programs for this computer.
agent.remote.no_install: SupportOne does not install any of these. It only looks for what is already here.
agent.remote.heading: %s is asking to connect to this computer. Here is what that lets them do:
agent.remote.will_start: SupportOne will start %s for you (%s). It will not set it up or connect it to anyone.
agent.remote.no_tool: SupportOne will not start anything. Open the remote-help program yourself when you are ready.
agent.remote.confirm: Type allow if you agree to all of the above, or press Enter to stop:
agent.remote.aborted: Nothing was started, and nobody was let in.
agent.remote.started: %s has been started. Give the technician the code it shows you, and nothing else.
agent.remote.start_it_yourself: Open the remote-help program now and give the technician the code it shows you.
agent.remote.not_watching: SupportOne is not part of what happens next and cannot see any of it.
agent.remote.press_enter: Press Enter when the session is over:
agent.remote.ended: The session was recorded as lasting %s.

agent.profile.does_not_conform: This computer does not meet the profile.
agent.profile.unanswered_counts_against: A check that could not answer is counted against the profile: certifying a machine nobody looked at would not be a certification.
ui.remote.none_installed: No remote-help program was found on this computer. You can still record the session here and open the program yourself.
ui.remote.no_install: SupportOne does not install any of these, and does not connect them to anyone. It starts a program you already have and writes down what you agreed to.

build.self_reported: That is what this copy says about itself, which is not proof: a changed copy would say whatever it was changed to say.
build.unsigned: This is a development build. Nobody published it, and there is nothing to check it against.
build.modified: This was built from a source tree with uncommitted changes, so it does not match any published version.
build.how_to_verify: To check a download really is what was published, verify it against SHA256SUMS and its signature. docs/RELEASE.md has the commands.
